newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Dead Sea speculative buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Dead Sea speculative buy.

text.p: Ofek Securities said in a report on Sunday it was maintaining its speculative buy recommendation for Israel's Dead Sea Works Ltd and increasing its earnings per share estimate for 1997 to $0.81.
The previous EPS estimate for 1997 was at $0.79. Ofek left unchanged its 1998 EPS estimate of $1.14.

Analyst Efraim Steinbruch said the company was continuing its preparations for the production of magnesium through its subsidiary Dead Sea Magnesium, a joint venture with Volkswagen, despite several difficulties in the manufacturing process.
"Company sources ascertain that most of the problematic issues have already been resolved, and the remaining ones will be addressed and resolved shortly," Steinbruch said.

"By the end of the year, the company will reach its full Stage 1 manufacturing capacity of 27 thousand tonnes per annum. Company losses for the first six months of the year total nearly $2 million. The expected annual loss of 1997, the plant's launch year, stands at $6 million," the report said.
"We expect the magnesium project will contribute significantly to Dead Sea's future profitability...until such time, however, company profitability will continue to be based upon potash sales."
Ofek maintained revenue for 1997 at an estimated $439.4 million and net income at $44.3 million. Revenue for 1998 is estimated at $530.8 million with net income at $62.4 million.
